correctness.rationale: For every positive rank-four Euler matrix A in the five Loginov–Orlov mutation classes, A is integral upper unitriangular, B=A+A^T has rank three, and T=-A^{-T}A satisfies T-I=-A^{-T}B. Left multiplication by a unimodular matrix preserves cokernel and Smith type. The source adjugate identity adj(B)=D(A)pp^T with primitive kernel p makes the gcd of the 3x3 minors exactly D(A), hence the order of the torsion cokernel. Independently used sympy Smith normal form (not the package verifier) for all five representative matrices, obtaining (1,1,22,0),(1,1,40,0),(1,3,18,0),(2,2,16,0),(1,1,72,0); all products of nonzero factors equal D=22,40,54,64,72. General all-class conclusion is conditional on the primary source stated adjugate and classification identities, not inferred merely from five examples.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge with a material source-access risk: Loginov–Orlov publicly classify the five degree-labeled mutation classes; the submitted claim is the integral Serre–Coxeter coinvariant interpretation and full Smith invariant factors. The numerical scalar degree of the source alone does not determine cyclic versus noncyclic torsion; for D=54 and 64 noncyclic structures were independently verified. Resultary nearest Euler pairing discriminant result concerns smooth surfaces and a different lattice quotient, not these rank-four T-I coinvariants. The primary Loginov–Orlov PDF was not accessible through arXiv/OA and authorized Oxford returned vpn_disconnected; abstract only cannot justify whole-paper noncoverage. Specific priority risk retained rather than automatic O rejection.
residual_risks: Most important: Loginov–Orlov arXiv:2609.39766 full paper was inaccessible; authorized Oxford retrieval yielded vpn_disconnected. Its uninspected text or appendices may state the same integral coinvariant result.

The torsion-order identity is an elementary formal consequence of source A,B,T and adjugate identities, so claim originality is focused on setting-specific interpretation and complete five-group Smith refinement, not on the general Smith minor theorem.
No categorical orbit construction or Grothendieck group beyond numerical rank-four matrices was proved.

value.rationale: PASS: T-I is a natural endomorphism of the integral numerical Grothendieck lattice. Its coinvariant torsion gives an intrinsic algebraic interpretation of the Euler-degree invariant that distinguishes mutation classes, while full Smith groups supply meaningful finite-group refinements, including noncyclic patterns for quadric and projective-space cases. The result is a natural exact invariant, not a new categorical orbit theorem or mutation-class classification.
